Root Guru · 根本上師

His Holiness Living Buddha Lian Sheng蓮生活佛　盧勝彥

Grandmaster Sheng-Yen Lu — founder of the True Buddha School, author of over three hundred books, and the root guru through whose blessing this sutra is taught and shared.

早年

Early life

His Holiness Living Buddha Lian Sheng was born Sheng-Yen Lu in 1945, in Chiayi, Taiwan, in the last months of the war, into a family that knew real poverty. As a child he sold popsicles and handmade toffee in the street; as a schoolboy he won a city-wide essay contest, and by his teens he was a published poet — nearly a thousand poems in the newspapers and his first book in print at seventeen. My life must have meaning, he wrote. I live not only for myself.

He worked his way through a surveying degree and served as an officer, living an outwardly ordinary life — until an afternoon that changed it entirely. At twenty-six, accompanying his mother to a temple in Taichung, his divine eye was opened in a sudden and overwhelming spiritual experience: the heavens revealed themselves, and he was shown that he was to cultivate the path and teach. From that day the invisible world never closed to him again.

修行

Training and lineages

What followed were years of intense cultivation across traditions — Christianity in his youth, then Taoism, Zen, Sutrayana and finally Tantrayana Buddhism — studying under accomplished teachers of each: three years under the unseen master San-Shan-Jiu-Hou, who gave him the dharma name Lian Sheng; the Taoist and Buddhist training of Master Qingzhen (Venerable Liaoming); and, from 1980, empowerments from His Holiness the 16th Karmapa of the Kagyu school, Master Sakya Zhengkong (Dezhung Rinpoche) of the Sakya, and Guru Thubten Dargye of the Gelug — so that he holds transmission in all four major lineages of Vajrayana Buddhism: Nyingma, Sakya, Kagyu and Gelug.

Through decades of actual practice he attained realization, and is revered by his students as an emanation of Amitabha Buddha — a Living Buddha who teaches from direct experience of the dharma rather than from books alone.

生平

Seven phases of a life

His students trace his life as seven phases — from an ordinary childhood in southern Taiwan to the teaching seat he still occupies every week.

1945–1968 平凡

The ordinary years

Born in Chiayi in the last months of the war, he grew up poor — a barefoot boy selling popsicles and toffee in the street — and grew into a gifted young writer: a prize essay in third grade, nearly a thousand published poems, a first book at seventeen.

1969–1984 學法

Learning the dharma

At twenty-six his divine eye was opened at a temple in Taichung. Three years under an unseen teacher gave him the name Lian Sheng and a vow he has never set down: "I will not attain buddhahood until hell is empty." Years of Taoist, Zen and Vajrayana training followed, and in 1982 he moved to Seattle.

1985–1988 弘法

Founding the True Buddha School

Weekly Heart Sutra talks in a Ballard attic grew into a school. In 1985 Ling Shen Ching Tze Temple was consecrated in Redmond — thunder rolled, it is remembered, as the temple plaque was raised — and in 1986 he received tonsure as a monk.

1989–1993 雲遊

Carrying the teaching across the world

He returned to Taiwan after seven years, and the teaching filled stadiums — Hong Kong, Taiwan, Southeast Asia — with ceremonies remembered for their healings. By forty-eight he had completed his hundredth book, writing as he travelled.

1994–2000 隱居

Withdrawing from the crowd

Announcing his seclusion in Vancouver, he stepped back from the stadiums to teach the inner tantras quietly, and set the school's affairs in order — the True Buddha Foundation was established in 1997. At the end of 2000 he left Seattle for a mountain retreat, taking almost nothing with him. "Retirement is only a change in form — what remains unchanged is my love for all sentient beings."

2001–2006 閉關

The long retreat

Six years in retreat and seclusion. Through grave illness he kept writing — close to a book a month — and made the sickness itself his practice, realizing, as he put it, that "the body is a prison", and deepening the realization of emptiness that marks his later teaching.

2007–today 大日再現

The great sun reappears

Emerging from retreat, he returned to the teaching seat — the Platform Sutra, the Hevajra commentary, the nine stages of Dzogchen, five years of Lamdre, the Vajra and Vimalakirti Sutras, and nightly deliverance ceremonies through the pandemic years. Since 2025 he has been expounding the Shurangama Sutra — still writing, still teaching, every week.

Chronology and photographs from A Hidden Sanctuary of the Living Buddha.

著作

Writings and teaching

His Holiness has written roughly three hundred books in Chinese — commentaries on the sutras and tantras, records of spiritual journeys, and plain-spoken guidance for cultivators — with many translated into English, Spanish, French, Vietnamese and other languages. He continues to write daily and to teach weekly, expounding sutra after sutra before assemblies in person and online.

It is in these very teachings that the Sutra of the Sea Dragon King was singled out and praised: The Dragon King Sutra is truly excellent — because it harmonises the Eight Classes of Heavenly and Dragon Beings. This website is offered in that spirit.

尊號

The name Lian Sheng

“Lian Sheng” (蓮生) means born of the lotus. To his students he is simply Shizun (師尊) — the revered teacher — or Grandmaster Lu. As the root guru of the True Buddha School he embodies the Triple Jewels for his disciples: the source of the lineage's blessing, empowerment and guidance.

Whoever sincerely takes refuge receives that transmission — and enters a stream of practice that leads, as this sutra itself promises, toward the realization of one's own true nature.
